title: Linear Momentum and Impulse
notes: **Linear momentum:** $\vec{p} = m\vec{v}$. It is a vector quantity pointing in the same direction as velocity.
**Impulse:** $\vec{J} = \vec{F}\Delta t$. Impulse equals the product of force and the time over which it acts.
**Impulse-Momentum Theorem:** $\vec{J} = \Delta\vec{p} = \vec{p}_f - \vec{p}_i$. The impulse delivered to an object equals the change in its momentum.

**Why impulse matters:** a large force acting for a short time can produce the same momentum change as a smaller force acting for a longer time. This is why airbags and crumple zones work â€” they increase the impact time, reducing the average force on passengers.
**Units:** momentum and impulse both have units of $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$ or $\text{N}\cdot\text{s}$.
